texts.preamble: Ajai Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 16 October, 2019 Author: Sudhir Agarwal Bench: Sudhir Agarwal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 34 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 597 of 1997 Revisionist :- Ajai Kumar
texts.arguments: It is contended by learned counsel for revisionist that revisionist was entitled for release by giving benefit of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1958") but Trial Court without considering this fact that applicant is first offender, convicted the applicant sentencing him to one year rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of 2,000/-. It is next contended that in the Ajai Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 20 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128605750/ 1 present matter, Trial Court neither invoked the "Act, 1958" nor provision of Section 360 Cr.P.C. by sentencing the accused-revisionist. In support of his contention, he has placed reliance upon the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Dhurukumar s/o Radhakishan Pitti and another vs. State of Maharashtra as well as order of this Court dated 15.5.2019 in Criminal Appeal No.745 of 2007 (Durgesh Chandra Vs. State of U.P.). The accused-revisionist has no criminal antecedents. Learned counsel for the revisionist further prayed for taking lenient view and extending the benefit of Section 4 of Act, 1958 to accused-revisionist. Learned A.G.A. has submitted that he has no objection and further submitted that accused-revisionist is not a previous convict.
texts.petitioner_arguments: It is contended by learned counsel for revisionist that revisionist was entitled for release by giving benefit of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1958") but Trial Court without considering this fact that applicant is first offender, convicted the applicant sentencing him to one year rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of 2,000/-. It is next contended that in the Ajai Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 20 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128605750/ 1 present matter, Trial Court neither invoked the "Act, 1958" nor provision of Section 360 Cr.P.C. by sentencing the accused-revisionist. In support of his contention, he has placed reliance upon the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Dhurukumar s/o Radhakishan Pitti and another vs. State of Maharashtra as well as order of this Court dated 15.5.2019 in Criminal Appeal No.745 of 2007 (Durgesh Chandra Vs. State of U.P.). The accused-revisionist has no criminal antecedents. Learned counsel for the revisionist further prayed for taking lenient view and extending the benefit of Section 4 of Act, 1958 to accused-revisionist.
texts.respondent_arguments: Learned A.G.A. has submitted that he has no objection and further submitted that accused-revisionist is not a previous convict.
